mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility has recovered about 25 points over four weeks and leads retail-and-recreation footfall; continued transit normalization pulls shoppers back to stores, so mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -39.1 at t-3w to -14.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its last-28-day mean despite TRANSIT continuing to rise for two more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has crossed above baseline, showing routine errand trips have resumed; resumed errand travel spills into adjacent retail and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM holds above 0 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -16.4 at t-3w to +6.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last-28-day mean within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM holds above zero.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling RESIDENTIAL (more people leaving home) and rising TRANSIT (more out-of-home trips) is the clearest signal of routine restoration; when both move together, retail footfall rises over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +3.0 in the same week that TRANSIT rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from 3.4 at t-2w to 2.6 at t-0w while TRANSIT rose from -31.1 to -14.0
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises simultaneously, RETAIL_REC is flat or lower over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stalled near -29 and stopped improving, capping weekday commuter-driven retail demand; with no further office return, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days stays below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change stays within plus or minus 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved only from -29.3 at t-1w to -29.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: plateaued reopening with offices still thin
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES remains flat within plus or minus 1 point for three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility peaked at +16.3 and has fallen to +11.9, indicating the outdoor-activity phase is fading; spending reallocates from outdoor recreation toward indoor retail venues within one week of the drop.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 3 points week-on-week from its four-week peak
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from +16.3 at t-1w to +11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop of more than 3 points from the four-week peak.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained above-baseline RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a persistent share of the population still staying home under residual restrictions; while RESIDENTIAL holds above +2, retail-and-recreation footfall is capped and the 28-day mean declines.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +2.0 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between +2.6 and +3.4 across all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +2.0 for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS combined with negative WORKPLACES marks a leisure-and-errand regime in which out-of-home trips are reallocated away from offices; this substitution sustains retail-and-recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 0 and PARKS above 0 in the same week while WORKPLACES remains below -20
regime_hint: substitution regime: offices thin, errands and leisure open
failure_condition: In weeks when GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are both positive and WORKPLACES is below -20, RETAIL_REC declines over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's four-week rebound has decelerated into a 1.2-point week-on-week decline at t-0w, the first negative step in the window; decelerating rebounds typically give back part of the gain, so the short-horizon mean falls.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC posts a negative week-on-week change after a four-week cumulative gain above 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC eased from -16.7 at t-1w to -17.9 at t-0w after gaining 20.4 points since t-3w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 7-day mean is higher than its t-0w value after a negative week-on-week print that followed a cumulative four-week gain above 15 points.
